references.text: Jesus' calling of the first disciples by the Sea of Galilee, where he finds fishermen working with nets and boats—a parallel account to the event in Luke 5.
Mark's account of the calling of the first disciples by the sea, where Jesus sees fishermen with boats and nets, paralleling Luke 5:2.
The disciples are out in the boat washing or casting nets, a similar scene where Jesus meets the fishermen by the sea after the resurrection.
The context for verse 2: the crowd presses in on Jesus at the Sea of Galilee, which explains why he sees the boats along the shore.
Jesus steps into one of the two boats mentioned in verse 2, namely Simon's boat, and asks him to push off from the shore.
Jesus uses a boat as a 'pulpit' by the sea to speak to the crowd, in a similar manner to Luke 5.
Prophecy about fishermen standing along the water and spreading out nets—an image that recalls the fishermen at the Sea of Galilee washing their nets.
